texto: Vocabulary of the family and kinship in Thai: the core terms are «พ่อ» (phɔ̂ɔ, father), «แม่» (mɛ̂ɛ, mother), «พี่» (phîi, older brother or sister) and «น้อง» (nɔ́ɔng, younger brother or sister). In Thai culture, relative age is crucial: there is no single common word for «brother or sister» that does not specify whether the sibling is older (พี่) or younger (น้อง). Moreover, these terms are used every day, warmly and politely, to address friends, colleagues or waiters according to their apparent age relative to you.
